constraints.statement: target(application_of(o))=o.application_ref; that application's traversal_ref and functor_kind_ref equal o's; target(applies_traversal(application_of(o).target))=o.traversal_ref; target(bound_to_subject(o))=o.subject_binding_ref; target(intends(o))=o.intended_outcome_ref. Targets of identity_depends_on with source o equal set(o.identity_dependency_refs). Sources of causally_precedes_occurrence with target o union sources of component_of_occurrence with target o equal set(o.lineage_refs). Lists, relation identities and exact (kind,source,target) triples must each be duplicate-free before set conversion; singleton relations exist exactly once. Duplicate, missing, extra, reversed or mismatched edges refuse occurrence_admission; a relation label cannot repair another identity preimage. Lineage contains only admitted occurrence-cause predecessors and aggregate component occurrences, never support, correction, timestamp, ordinal, adjacency or correlation edges. Identity, causal, support, correction, component, frontier-membership and evidence relations are finite and duplicate-free. Inverse is explicit; silence implies none.

conditions: Each constraint is evaluated only on its named record kind within its declared scope.

grounding.quote:
Every constraint predicate returns exactly one of `satisfied`,
`falsified`, `indeterminate` or `invalid_basis`.

constraints.statement: Closed constraint kinds: identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic, event_causation_acyclic, occurrence_seed_complete, relation_claim_admissible, semantic_cut_complete, pre_effect_current, operation_grant_contains_effect, event_scope_compatible, frontier_complete, transition_subject_complete. Closed judgment kinds: model_validation, occurrence_admission, event_admission, claim_admission, semantic_cut_admission, effect_readiness, transition_evaluation, frontier_projection. Closed residual kinds: unobserved_subject_state, partial_effect, unresolved_cause, unresolved_scope, competing_lineage, stale_frontier, stale_currentness, unobserved_external_mutation. Closed stop kinds: hold, gap, refusal, invalid_basis, out_of_scope, partial_effect. Constraint predicates return exactly satisfied, falsified, indeterminate or invalid_basis, excluding out_of_frame because evaluation stays inside applies_to. satisfied maps to the first listed judgment decision, invalid_basis only to invalid_basis; other mappings are fixed below. Event scope conflicting with admission authority falsifies event_scope_compatible; its out_of_scope stop is distinct from out_of_frame. No omitted result, residual or stop becomes success. FunctorKind contains exact b_ac references F_D, F_P and F_H only, with unchanged imported laws.

grounding.quote: | `effect_readiness` | `EffectSubject` | `ready`, `stale`, `unauthorized`, `hold`, `invalid_basis` | exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory, and invalidation state | stale yields `hold` plus `stale_currentness` and re-observation; unauthorized yields `refusal` and no dispatch |

constraints.statement: model_validation: unchanged OccurrenceModelSubject; decisions valid/hold/refused/invalid_basis; evidence exact model id/digest, profile basis, typed graph populations; refusal or invalid basis, with unresolved references retaining gap until repaired. occurrence_admission: Occurrence; admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis; exact occurrence id/digest and resolved pre-existing seed inputs; missing seed retains hold+unresolved_cause, re-entry is a new complete occurrence candidate. event_admission: FrameworkEvent; admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis/out_of_scope; exact event id/digest, payload digest, scope authority and source frontier; unresolved scope retains hold+unresolved_scope, incompatible scope refuses. claim_admission: RelationClaim; admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis; exact claim id/digest, endpoints, qualifiers, claimant authority and current source frontier; unresolved cause or stale frontier retains hold, re-entry is a new claim over current frontier. semantic_cut_admission: SemanticAdmissionCut; admitted/hold/refused/invalid_basis; exact seven-member cut and source/successor frontier equality; incomplete/inconsistent cut refuses, stale source retains hold+stale_frontier and requires reconstruction. effect_readiness: EffectSubject; ready/stale/unauthorized/hold/invalid_basis; exact pre-observation, invocation, operation, grant, territory and invalidation state; stale yields hold+stale_currentness with re-observation, unauthorized yields refusal and no dispatch. transition_evaluation: TransitionSubject; satisfied/falsified/partial/indeterminate/refused/invalid_basis; exact pre/post observations, intended outcome, disposition and bounded evidence; partial yields partial_effect, indeterminate retains hold+declared residual, refused yields refusal. frontier_projection: Projection; admitted/hold/gap/refused/invalid_basis; exact projection/frontier ids/digests, complete members, basis, precedence law, boundary and residuals; stale retains hold+stale_frontier, unresolved lineage retains gap, re-entry is a new projection. Each judgment retains inherited unchanged-subject, evaluator, authority, evidence, provenance and decision coordinates; stops and residuals are determined by kind, not inferred from prose.

grounding.quote: | `event_scope_compatible` | `FrameworkEvent` | `event_admission` | `out_of_scope` plus `refusal` | `hold` plus `unresolved_scope` |

constraints.statement: Exact subject/judgment/falsified/indeterminate mappings: identity_dependency_acyclic, occurrence_causation_acyclic and event_causation_acyclic each use OccurrenceModelSubject/model_validation/refused+refusal/hold+unresolved_cause. occurrence_seed_complete uses Occurrence/occurrence_admission/refused+refusal/hold+unresolved_cause. relation_claim_admissible uses RelationClaim/claim_admission/refused+refusal/hold+(unresolved_cause or stale_frontier). semantic_cut_complete uses SemanticAdmissionCut/semantic_cut_admission/refused+refusal/hold+stale_frontier. pre_effect_current uses EffectSubject/effect_readiness/stale+hold+stale_currentness/hold+stale_currentness. operation_grant_contains_effect uses EffectSubject/effect_readiness/unauthorized+refusal/hold+unobserved_subject_state. event_scope_compatible uses FrameworkEvent/event_admission/out_of_scope+refusal/hold+unresolved_scope. frontier_complete uses Projection/frontier_projection/refused+refusal/hold+stale_frontier. transition_subject_complete uses TransitionSubject/transition_evaluation/refused+refusal/indeterminate+unobserved_subject_state.

grounding.quote:
| `stale_currentness` | `EffectSubject` | re-observe and re-judge before effect |
| `unobserved_external_mutation` | `SubjectBinding` | observe or retain an explicit material unknown |

constraints.statement: Residual kind fixes subject and re-entry: unobserved_subject_state→SubjectBinding, acquire bounded observation or retain hold; partial_effect→EffectInvocation, acquire post-observation and explicit disposition; unresolved_cause→claim or event, acquire authority and evidence or retain unresolved; unresolved_scope→FrameworkEvent, declare lawful scope or refuse admission; competing_lineage→EventFrontier, apply authorized frontier_projection judgment; stale_frontier→Projection, construct new exact frontier and projection; stale_currentness→EffectSubject, re-observe and re-judge before effect; unobserved_external_mutation→SubjectBinding, observe or retain explicit material unknown.

grounding.quote:
A judgment decision is the evaluation's result and a stop is the step's.
Where values emitted together map to different core values, as `stale`
with `hold` does, each answers its own predicate.

constraints.statement: Judgment mapping predicate: the first listed decision holds for the unchanged subject on the exact basis. Stop mapping predicate: the traversal application can reach its declared result on the exact basis, distinct from construction availability ('a candidate is available'). Effect-disposition predicate: the intended effect occurred, when applicable. Each emitted value answers only its own predicate, even when co-emitted values have different core results. Stops map hold→indeterminate; gap→invalid_basis because required reference/lineage closure is unresolved; refusal(constraint)→falsified; refusal(basis)→invalid_basis; invalid_basis→invalid_basis; out_of_scope→falsified; partial_effect(not_attained)→falsified; partial_effect(undecided)→indeterminate. Decisions map partial(not_attained)→falsified; partial(undecided)→indeterminate; refused(constraint)→falsified; refused(basis)→invalid_basis. Each judgment's first decision maps satisfied; out_of_scope, unauthorized and stale map falsified; hold maps indeterminate; gap maps invalid_basis; invalid_basis, falsified and indeterminate retain their namesake core values. out_of_scope is emitted only with refusal for declared scope conflicting with admitting authority, not for an undeclared event scope; while unresolved, that case is hold+unresolved_scope. Core mappings preserve original vocabulary, residuals and re-entry and cannot be remapped by individual traversals.

grounding.quote:
- `refusal(constraint)`: every other refusal, that is, every refusal that
  names a demonstrated violation by what is under judgment, whatever
  condition of the basis it also names, or names no condition that AC-007
  lists for `refusal(basis)`.

constraints.statement: Refusal cause is determined by named conditions under the cited AC-007, not chosen by qualifier or structural location. refusal(basis) names only conditions of the operation's basis and no demonstrated violation by the object under judgment; violations inside an input acted on as basis count as basis conditions. A basis-only coordinate/basis mismatch, model/record basis-relation mismatch, qualifier mismatch or cross-basis cut edge is mixed bases, not a structural counterexample. If a qualifier records this cause it is refuse_invalid_basis. refusal(constraint) covers every other refusal: a demonstrated violation by the judged record/model/carrier/transformation/application, even with a basis condition, or no condition eligible for refusal(basis). Qualifiers recording it use refuse_missing/refuse_duplicate/refuse_wrong_type/refuse_out_of_scope. Named accompanying basis conditions and co-emitted invalid_basis decisions retain their own invalid_basis result. refused(basis/constraint) follows its yielded refusal's cause. Structural counterexamples include unknown/missing fields; missing populations, hidden records, ambiguous refs, unknown kinds, undeclared domains; reference/cardinality/nested-coordinate defects; event-kind/payload/digest/forbidden-field defects; qualifier/closed-union defects; and duplicate/missing/extra/reversed/mismatched edges. A scope still undeclared when unresolved_scope re-entry closes is a demonstrated event defect: refusal(constraint), retained unresolved_scope, and re-entry through a new lawfully scoped event candidate. It is not the out_of_scope stop. Open resolution retains gap; a reference evaluated to no target, including a missing local record, is dangling and refuses. Qualifier defect distinctions remain alongside the core value.

conditions: For partial_effect stops/dispositions and partial transition decisions.

grounding.quote:
A lost response, an absent record or an
  actor's context holding no trace of the effect is no evidence about the
  subject, so it establishes neither non-attainment nor the end of the
  effect

constraints.statement: not_attained requires admitted effect evidence and bounded post-observation, interpreted under intended outcome contract and comparison basis, establishing both that the outcome is unmet and that no later completion can meet it. Examples include an effect ended short, a bounded interval closed partially attained, or an irreversible performed part defeating the outcome. Whether the effect ended is not part of this cause; unestablished end remains a residual. undecided covers every other partial_effect: no bounded post-observation yet, partial progress with completion still possible, currently met outcome with still-acting effect, or lost response without observed counterexample. Lost response, missing record or absent actor trace establishes neither non-attainment nor effect end. partial decisions inherit the cause of their partial_effect stop; missing required post-observation under transition_subject_complete remains indeterminate+unobserved_subject_state. Neither falsified nor indeterminate records actual mutation or end; partial_effect residual and re-entry carry these through every join. Falsified cannot imply no effect; indeterminate cannot imply no effect or completion; neither implies ended without evidence. Explicit re-entry precedes every further effect; an effect of unestablished end is reconciled under cited ACTIVATION §5 before repetition.

grounding.quote:
A
retry or a continuation creates a fresh occurrence only when it reapplies
the traversal.

constraints.statement: Only pre-admission facts enter occurrence identity. Post-effect observations, effect evidence, judgments, admitted events, timestamps, admission ordinals and projection results are excluded; they may reference the occurrence after their own identities exist. Application identity is exact and pre-existing; application traversal/functor fields equal occurrence fields. Lineage and identity-dependency inputs are precisely the congruence-law populations; relation records are minted after occurrence identity and reproduce its endpoints rather than seed it. Two applications of one traversal over one subject are distinct occurrences. Retry/continuation creates a fresh occurrence only upon traversal reapplication; a later controller step, observation, wait or correlation record is insufficient. Every retained bracketed AC-016 traversal application gets an occurrence; an applied declared composite also gets an aggregate. Components point to aggregate via component_of_occurrence without implied material cause. Intermediate results, judgments, evidence, authority, provenance and stops remain explicit.

grounding.quote:
The directed graph formed by `identity_depends_on` is finite and acyclic.
Every dependency target exists before the dependent identity is minted. A
future result or event cannot be smuggled into its own occurrence seed

constraints.statement: identity_depends_on forms a finite DAG. Every target exists before minting its dependent identity. A future result or event cannot enter its own occurrence seed.

conditions: For relation-claim admission.

grounding.quote:
Only `j_c.decision = admitted`, `j_e.decision = admitted` and
`j_a.decision = admitted` together admit the complete semantic cut.

constraints.statement: Described sequence: claim c; claim_admission judgment j_c over unchanged c; candidate event e binding c,j_c,source F_k; event_admission judgment j_e over unchanged e; deterministic relation r from (c,j_c,e,j_e,basis); successor frontier; seven-member cut a; semantic_cut_admission judgment j_a over unchanged a. Admission requires all three judgments admitted. c,j_c,e,j_e,r,a,j_a have distinct identities and authority. Constructing c does not admit it; judgments do not rewrite subjects; events do not inherit candidate authority. Materialisation preserves accepted kind, endpoints, qualifiers and basis. Each j_c/j_e/j_a has its exact kind, respective subject id and sha256(canonical subject bytes), complete inherited context, owner, scope, basis, evaluator, authority, decision, evidence, provenance and decision-time fields. Missing cut judgment, non-admitted decision, wrong subject/digest or cross-basis judgment refuses the cut.

conditions: For a claim-admission cut.

grounding.quote:
The source frontier must not
already contain `e`, and duplicate frontier members refuse before any set
comparison (P3, P5).

constraints.statement: Admission-event identity binds event kind, payload digest, scope, optional occurrence, exact claim and claim judgment, source frontier, owner and basis. Materialized relation identity binds unchanged claim, claim judgment, event, event judgment and profile basis. frontier_contains(F,e) iff e occurs exactly once in F.member_event_refs, with no extras or omissions. Event kind is exact claim-admission URN; claim/event/cut source_frontier_ref values are identical. Each cut reference resolves the unchanged judged/materialized record. All seven cut subjects, all three judgments and three required relation records share exact profile basis. Frontiers share projection_basis_ref and precedence_law_ref; only successor difference is adding e.id once. Required edges are exactly admits_claim(e,c), materializes_relation(e,r), frontier_contains(successor,e), with inherited relation shape and exact qualifiers. Missing, extra, reversed, duplicate or cross-basis required edges refuse; source must not already contain e; frontier duplicates refuse before set comparison. First event requires no fictional predecessor. Re-admission with same claim, claim judgment, event judgment, source frontier, basis and authority returns existing byte-equal cut; nonidentical collision refuses with refuse_duplicate and creates no rival facts. Claim endpoints pre-exist; generated admission/materialization edges are post-admission relations, never self-future-endpoint claims.

conditions: For a relation claim.

grounding.quote:
Missing,
conflicting or inconsistent members refuse the cut. This atomicity is
semantic; the profile prescribes no storage or transaction mechanism

constraints.statement: One admitted cut contains unchanged claim and admission judgment, event with scope and admission judgment, deterministic relation, exact common source frontier and unique successor equal to source plus exactly the admitted event. Missing, conflicting or inconsistent members refuse. Atomicity is semantic and prescribes no storage or transaction mechanism.

conditions: When corrects_event(new,existing) holds.

grounding.quote:
`corrects_event(new, existing)` keeps both immutable events. A correction
changes later projection through an explicit selection law; it does not
delete, rewrite or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact

constraints.statement: Both events remain immutable. Correction affects later projection only through explicit selection law; it does not delete, rewrite or retrospectively re-identify the corrected fact.

grounding.quote:
Each is acyclic under its own typed relation. Cause is established only by
an admitted causal claim under competent authority and evidence.

constraints.statement: Identity-dependency, occurrence-causation and event-causation graphs remain distinct and each acyclic under its own typed relation. Cause requires admitted causal claim, competent authority and evidence. Timestamp, ordinal, adjacency, containment, shared subject, shared actor, correlation and arrival order create no cause. An untyped-union cycle is not a causal cycle unless a declared causal subgraph itself cycles.

conditions: When projection uses precedence to select current truth.

grounding.quote:
The coordinate, its comparison law, its basis and its admitting
authority are explicit. The coordinate orders eligible facts; it gains no
semantic, admission, causal or decision authority

constraints.statement: Precedence coordinate, comparison law, basis and admitting authority must be explicit. The coordinate orders eligible facts and gains no semantic, admission, causal or decision authority.

exceptions: An adopting Product may replace exact territory equality only by an explicit authority-owned containment relation in its compatible signature.

grounding.quote:
No operation is lawful without a matching grant that names the subject
binding, the operation kind and the effect territory.

constraints.statement: Functor kind, traversal, domain operation, executor, actor, grant and invocation are different coordinates. F_P/F_D/F_H classification alone neither identifies, authorizes nor executes an operation; profile construction and occurrence admission mint no grant. Every lawful operation requires an exact owner-issued matching grant. invocation.operation_ref=operation.id; target(operation_of_kind(operation))=operation.operation_kind_ref; target(targets_subject(operation))=operation.subject_binding_ref; target(authorized_by(invocation))=invocation.operation_grant_ref=grant.id. Operation, grant and occurrence subject bindings are equal; operation kind belongs to grant.allowed_operation_kind_refs; operation contract equals the exact OperationKind object's contract; operation, invocation and grant territory values are equal. Same label with different contract/target sort, invalidated kind or unresolved kind reference cannot be authorized by the grant. Nominal kind equality, role label, executor access and broad workspace access are insufficient.

grounding.quote:
`j_ready` judges the unchanged `EffectSubject` immediately before effect
dispatch under the application's declared currentness and invalidation
law.

constraints.statement: Described effect sequence observes W under stable binding, constructs exact invocation and readiness subject, judges readiness immediately before dispatch, dispatches when ready, obtains later disposition and bounded post-observation, then judges TransitionSubject. unauthorized or stale readiness never dispatches; invokes_effect exists iff a concrete invocation was dispatched. Stale pre-observation or grant prevents starting: re-observe and issue new readiness subject/judgment or stop. no_effect has no dispatched invocation and records no attempted domain effect. completed_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation and sufficient evidence. partial_effect binds one dispatched invocation, bounded post-observation/evidence, partial_effect residual and stop, and explicit re-entry before further effect. refused_effect binds refused invocation attempt and refusal stop with evidence that no authorized mutation began. A begun effect lacking complete disposition keeps partial_effect explicit and requires bounded post-observation. Invocation is immutable and lacks future disposition; later disposition does not rewrite it. No lock or transaction implementation is required.

conditions: An EffectInvocation names the occurrence, thereby making it intend an effect.
exceptions: If no EffectInvocation names the occurrence, no effect is intended: no_effect is only a record of no attempted domain effect, not an effect result.

grounding.quote:
An occurrence that no `EffectInvocation` names intends no effect.
ACTIVATION §3 Effects poses no predicate for it, and its `no_effect`
records only that no domain effect was attempted: it is a record, not an
effect result

constraints.statement: For predicate 'the intended effect occurred': completed_effect→completed→satisfied requires bounded observation and sufficient evidence establishing occurrence and end; partial_effect(not_attained)→not_effected→falsified requires unmet and unattainable-by-later-completion outcome, retaining actual occurred part and unestablished end beside the value; partial_effect(undecided)→completion_unknown→indeterminate; refused_effect→not_effected→falsified because evidence shows no authorized mutation began; no_effect→not_effected→falsified because exact admitted disposition records no dispatched invocation. Applicability is not inferred for occurrences intending no effect.

conditions: For a later traversal application when authority is unchanged.

grounding.quote:
A later traversal application observes the then-current
`W` under the stable binding when authority is unchanged

constraints.statement: Observe then-current W under stable binding. Observation, evidence, result, checkpoint, event, projection, cache and model content may describe W but none replaces it. A new occurrence implies no rollback.

conditions: On traversal reapplication.

grounding.quote:
Iteration does not mutate an earlier occurrence. Each traversal
reapplication mints a fresh immutable occurrence over the evolving
subject, so the admitted occurrence and event history is append-only even
when the external subject changes repeatedly

constraints.statement: Reapplication mints a fresh immutable occurrence over the evolving subject; it never mutates an earlier occurrence. Admitted occurrence and event histories remain append-only despite repeated external mutation.

grounding.quote:
New events create a new frontier, and a prior projection does not silently
advance. Latest-only summaries do not prove frontier completeness.

constraints.statement: For each exact profile basis b, scope s and precedence law p there is one empty frontier F_0(b,s,p). Admitting e constructs successor membership exactly members(F_k) union {e}. Frontier identity binds basis/scope/precedence law/sorted event ids/content digests; projection identity binds exact frontier, rule, selected relation/boundary/residual ids. Judgment binds unchanged projection id/digest and each projection exactly one unchanged frontier. New events create new frontiers without silently advancing prior projections. Latest-only summaries prove no completeness. Competing corrections, unresolved scope, missing causal inputs and stale basis remain residuals or stops under selected projection law.

grounding.quote:
Every event carries its declared scope class. `event_for` is present only
when the scope law names one exact occurrence. Facts that are
subject-wide, publication-wide or otherwise independent of any occurrence
stay independent

constraints.statement: Every event declares scope class. event_for is present only where scope law names one exact occurrence. Subject-wide, publication-wide and otherwise occurrence-independent facts remain independent.

grounding.quote:
An absent or incomplete adoption means the profile is available but
inactive for that Product

constraints.statement: Profile grants no semantic, operation, evaluation, admission, decision, correction, continuation or closure authority. Every material operation/judgment resolves an existing owner-issued grant; copying records or adopting transfers none. Only Product authority adopts. Adoption declares at least exact profile basis; exact subject/binding interpretation; Product-concept mappings to sorts and relation kinds; operation/actor/executor/admission/projection/decision authorities; event-scope/frontier laws; invalidation/re-entry conditions; and qualification evidence that no Product distinction was lost. Absent/incomplete adoption leaves the profile available but inactive for that Product.

conditions: Once publication bytes exist.

grounding.quote:
The list is free of duplicates and sorted by ascending unsigned
UTF-16 code units.

constraints.statement: TraversalOccurrenceSignature has kind='stdo.traversal-occurrence-signature', schema_version=1, exact calculus_basis_identity, calculus_signature_schema_clause_ref, occurrence_signature_clause_refs and profile_member_sha256. Signature identity is sha256(JCS(signature)) using RFC 8785. Occurrence clause refs are a sorted nonempty duplicate-free absolute URI list, ascending unsigned UTF-16, resolving exactly publication-member fragments #authority-and-adoption, #candidate-judgment-event-and-relation-separation, #causality-and-typed-lineage, #closed-constraint-judgment-residual-and-stop-kinds, #closed-event-kind-population, #closed-relation-families, #closed-semantic-object-sorts, #event-frontier-and-projection, #mutable-subject-effect-relation, #occurrence-identity. Their base equals exact member_uri. Calculus clause resolves inherited signature schema/record law inside exact calculus publication, #2-signature in this corpus. profile_member_sha256 equals publication member digest. Relative paths, mutable source URIs, missing fragments, duplicate refs or refs outside the two exact publication members refuse signature. The closed signature has one reconstructable preimage and no implementation-defined serialization.

grounding.quote:
The signature and basis preimages are their
exact RFC 8785 JCS values; a newline, another object order, a duplicate
name, a value outside I-JSON or an implementation-specific serialisation
cannot acquire the declared identity

constraints.statement: Basis kind='stdo.traversal-occurrence-profile-basis', schema_version=1, concept_identity='urn:stdo:concept:traversal-occurrence-profile'; fields also include exact calculus_basis_identity, embedded occurrence_signature, occurrence_signature_sha256 and publication_basis={release_uri,manifest_sha256,member_uri,member_sha256}. Signature digest equals embedded canonical signature digest. Basis identity is 'urn:stdo:traversal-occurrence-profile-basis:sha256:' + sha256(JCS(basis)); duplicate object names are rejected before canonicalization. release_uri is absolute immutable stdo://releases/v<version>-rc.<positive-ordinal>/; member_uri is exactly release_uri+'standards/TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md'. Installed manifest contains that path and digest exactly once; digest also equals embedded signature's member digest. All digests use lowercase sha256:<64-hex>; kind/schema values and RFC8785/I-JSON preimages are exact. Noncanonical bytes, newline, other object ordering, duplicate names or custom serialization cannot acquire declared identity. Any change to calculus basis, signature refs, closed signature or member bytes mints a new basis. Supersession is an external Product/release judgment; old bases never silently advance. Predecessor rc.2 TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE.md digest 618bb7c8f9f1eab8283cf595ac9da3533f0f9cf80a684c6f42e09142da6590c1 is provenance, not this edition's identity; concept identity is unchanged.

grounding.quote:
A string of
the right shape, an unresolved basis record, a mismatched manifest or
member, a missing or extra principle ref, an invented or absent fragment,
an unbound predecessor byte sequence, or a derivation from the same
carrier refuses

constraints.statement: Imported AxiomaticCalculusBasis resolves exact RFC8785 bytes with required kind/schema/concept/derivation/publication basis; calculated identity equals both calculus_basis_identity fields. Its manifest digest resolves exact bytes containing calculus member path/digest once; member bytes match. Signature clause URI is exact calculus member plus applicable heading fragment. Distinct predecessor manifest resolves every sorted duplicate-free principle ref inside declared predecessor release. Principle population is exactly absolute predecessor-release expansion of every derivation address declared by the bound calculus member, neither subset nor invented list; size follows its derivation account. Each predecessor member's exact bytes have a digest appearing once in manifest; each fragment resolves one heading under publication semantic-address law. Merely shaped strings, unresolved basis, mismatched manifest/member, missing/extra principle refs, invented/absent fragment, unbound predecessor bytes or same-carrier derivation refuse. Profile publication uses the same manifest/member rule. Mutable source paths, strategy posts, implementations and consumer mappings cannot substitute for imported basis or publication identity.
constraints.uncertainty: Required publication and predecessor bytes are not supplied.

constraints.statement: Profile is not a change to pure a_c/reference-frame law; mandatory for every symbolic model; concrete subject/workspace ontology; process/traversal/retry/continuation/closure engine; event store/log schema/projection implementation/state carrier; mutation/admission/evaluation/decision authority; prospective-frame/sensor-population profile; guarantee that every event belongs to an occurrence; or assertion that every typed lineage graph is acyclic.

conditions: For review and qualification.

grounding.quote:
Representative examples or checkers establish only the claims they
actually evaluate. They do not become an occurrence engine or a semantic
authority

constraints.statement: Review/qualification cover at least all 21 cases: one exact a_c basis/eight-member RecordKind_ac function/closed domains without inherited-field shadowing; exact inherited families/direct coordinates/disjoint local-external identities; complete seeds/congruence/future-input refusal; first event without fictional predecessor; distinct candidate/judgment/event/relation/cut/cut-judgment identities and subject digest; idempotent-or-refused duplicate admission; cycles in each identity/causal subgraph; lawful opposing support/correction; closed event kinds/payload/digest/scope/bindings and independent events without fabricated event_for; separation of functor/traversal/operation kind/instance/executor/actor/grant/invocation/target/territory; missing/stale/mismatched/out-of-territory grants; all four effect cases; mutable reality carrier; fresh reapplication identity; component/aggregate identities; refusal on stale pre-observation and grant currentness; incomplete semantic batch refusal including missing/non-admitted cut judgment and unequal source frontiers; frontier completeness/staleness/correction selection; non-causation by timestamp/ordinal/adjacency/containment/correlation; absent adoption and incomplete-mapping refusal; exact JCS/kinds/schemas/immutable URIs/digests/calculus address/unique-membership basis reconstruction. Examples/checkers establish only evaluated claims, not engine or semantic authority.
constraints.uncertainty: The checklist's stale-readiness 'refusal' wording is retained alongside the more specific stale/hold law, without equating them.

exceptions: The fourteen-member predecessor count is marked superseded only as proposed and pending Product-owner acceptance.

grounding.quote:
Three clauses have no predecessor row and are new: the mapping of the
judgment decisions and stop kinds to the core result algebra

constraints.statement: The account claims all 25 predecessor rows conserved at predecessor modal force, with formal tables/code exact and surrounding prose rewritten; routes are provenance only and heading slugs preserve ten signature fragments. It attributes successor member path/calculus fragment and profile ownership of instantiate_signature, OccurrenceSignatureDefinition, Sigma:ReferenceDomain/ExternalTargetKind/BasisRelation as generalizations; British spelling changes prose only. New clauses are judgment/stop core mappings, effect-disposition mappings and foundation-family table. Conserved coverage explicitly includes position/URNs, scope, inherited boundary, nineteen sorts, complete reference table/expansion, four event kinds, 24 relation kinds/qualifiers/cardinality/congruence, closed kind populations/tables, identity, admission separation, seven OP laws, causality, effects, frontier, adoption, edition/signature, exclusions and 21 conformance obligations. Source account repeats cause-sensitive mappings and open-gap versus dangling distinction; these remain the rules stated in their owning supplied sections. The synthetic child row proposes replacing the edition-specific fourteen principle-ref count with size derived from exact bound calculus account, retaining the population law; acceptance remains pending.
constraints.uncertainty: Conservation and proposed supersession are source claims, not verified comparison or acceptance.

conditions: For UX surfaces governed by this profile.

grounding.quote:
